title: Fourth-round parallel render and automation preparation reductions
scope: Interaction and render preparation after editor admission; editor startup and expected web lazy loading excluded.

findings.change: Use dependency counts and a numeric heap instead of repeatedly scanning every task until its dependencies have been visited.
findings.evidence: 600 seeded DAG/worker combinations and 12,288 exhaustive four-node digraph/worker comparisons retain exact former pass/index order and refusals. A 120-task reverse chain reads dependency lists at most 360 times; the original reads more than 6000.
findings.limitations: This is the private parallel worker-plane compiler, separate from round3's lexical PDC vertex frontier.

findings.change: Prepare authored-order VCA products once per admitted member instead of scanning every VCA membership list for every parallel strip.
findings.evidence: 1500 queries over 30 members add no membership reads after preparation; duplicate members apply once, authored .1 times .3 remains exact, and master gain remains one.
findings.limitations: Invocation-local preparation for parallel stack tasks; separate from the live AudioNode controls optimized in round3.

findings.change: Resolve tap scope from a first-authority group/send catalog rather than scanning both node collections per strip.
findings.evidence: Group-before-send duplicate authority, master/track cases and unknown-node cue fallback are checked; all 144 complete-plan/refusal hashes match the original.
findings.limitations: Scope determines the private worker tap-plane directory, not the graph channel-width index from round3.

findings.change: Traverse the solo strip Set directly instead of spreading it into a fresh array for each parallel strip audibility query.
findings.evidence: The integrated compiler matches 123 complete plans and 21 exact refusals, including seeded solo, VCA mute, nested group and cue routes.
findings.limitations: Topology queries and early-return order are preserved; this removes the repeated array allocation and does not memoize mutable audibility.

findings.change: Reuse one groups/sends/cues list for owner preparation, solo discovery and stack construction instead of concatenating the same collections three times.
findings.evidence: Complete compiled plan hashes preserve owner, solo and stack order at 32, 44.1 and 48 kHz with 1–8 workers.
findings.limitations: This is one shared concatenation cost, counted once across its three consumers.

findings.change: Reuse the compiler's private filtered dense effect array as the compiled inventory, avoiding a second map result allocation.
findings.evidence: Tests retain all flag inspection before compilation, caller record/array identity and authored compilation error order. Exotic caller-owned filter/map authority retains the former fallback.
findings.limitations: Only the new private dense array is overwritten; caller-owned racks are never mutated.

findings.change: Record EQ presence while compiling admitted effects, removing the subsequent compiled-rack some traversal.
findings.evidence: The exotic-map fixture retains a true EQ presence result. Frozen complete compiler refusals include unprepared EQ module admission and unsupported effects in the original order.
findings.limitations: Presence is a separate downstream admission query from latency and array allocation; no EQ engine bytes change.

findings.change: Sum compiled effect latency in the authored compilation loop, removing the later reduce traversal.
findings.evidence: Two limiter effects retain exact 48 + 96 = 144-frame rack latency at 48 kHz. Complete plans, PDC offsets and refusal hashes retain their original values.
findings.limitations: Addition order remains authored order; global PDC solving remains unchanged.

findings.change: Lazily prepare a first-match effect ID catalog for queried parallel tasks instead of finding the rack again for each sidechain edge.
findings.evidence: 500 repeated sidechain lookups add no effect ID reads after the first query; unqueried racks are not indexed, missing IDs and duplicate first authority are checked.
findings.limitations: The catalog belongs to one finished plan build and never survives parameter/rack mutation.

findings.change: Capture the fixed normalized window inputs and sampleRate * transportRate divisor once per real AudioParam scheduling window instead of rereading and multiplying them for every event.
findings.evidence: Red/green fixed-input getters for 1,000 projections fall from 4,000 to 4 total reads. The 100 complete actual registerAudioParam/group call/error fixtures preserve Float64 time/value bytes: 48 single and 48 composite rate/sample-rate/latency combinations plus 4 partial-failure cases. Continuing and overlapping cancellation and transform/param/cancel exceptions match captured original registry SHA256 93fc51563930965aac579a670cc83d84474702017b9ba3e5fc49c8dc191d7d65. All 24 focused scheduling tests pass, including 157 standalone conversion/refusal fixtures.
findings.limitations: Only immutable normalized registry windows use the timing helper. Original parentheses remain contextStartTime + (latencySeconds + (frame-fromFrame)/(sampleRate*transportRate)); multiplication is prepared without reciprocal reassociation. Extreme rates retain Infinity/NaN times and original AudioParam behavior. Cancellation, binding/event order and partial-failure frontier publication remain unchanged. Standalone conversion extraction and restored future message targets add no counted cost. Root owns representative timing and final gates.

rejectedCandidates.reason: Current Soundscaper registers AudioParam bindings. The message-target producer is a future contract with no current production caller; packet-factor retention and its unused public factory were removed. Per-event standalone message conversion is restored; its 157 compatibility fixtures remain uncounted protection.

audioParamParity.method: Independent esbuild bundle substitutes only captured original registry bytes while resolving unchanged owning imports. Maintained helper records complete public calls/errors with exact Float64 time/value bytes; equality is checked outside timers. Temporary generator recipe/provenance: /tmp/perf300-generate-audio-param-parity.mjs and /tmp/perf300-audio-param-parity-provenance.json.
